newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to drop fiscal incentives in '97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to drop fiscal incentives in '97 - paper.

text.p: Next year, Mexico plans to drop certain fiscal incentives for businesses that were introduced this year to ease hardships of the recession and stimulate growth, Mexico City daily El Economista said Friday.

Citing unnamed sources from the Finance Ministry, the daily said extended the incentives program would cost the government 19.7 billion pesos, so it has been decided to abandon certain schemes to boost revenues.

From January 1, 1997, Mexicans will again have to pay the asset tax of 1.8 percent and taxes on purchases of new vehicles, and tax deductions on investments and fleet car purchases will be scrapped, El Economista said.
To compensate, the Finance Ministry plans to extend debt payment periods and also speed up tax rebates.
The measures will be debated at this weekend's renewal of the annual "pacto" between government, business and labour leaders. The pact is Mexico's mechanism to control inflation and wage hikes.
